input.brief: Kultura: a dark, image-first library of everything you watch, read and play (movies, series, anime, manga, games, books, comics); covers speak, few words

direction.name: The contact sheet
direction.idea: Show everything at once, small, in order. The work is laid out like a photographer's contact sheet or an archive drawer: dozens of small frames in strict rows, with all text set at one small size. Nothing is featured, which is the point: the volume and consistency of the body of work is the statement, and the visitor does the choosing. It suits people and studios whose strength is range and output.
direction.composition: The name, or one sentence about the work, sits at display size (6–9vw) across the top of the first screen, and the sheet begins directly under it, still inside the first screen. The first screen opens with three or four short blocks of small text across the top on a 12-column grid (who, what, where to reach them), all at 14–16px, and immediately below, the sheet begins: rows of thumbnails at a fixed height (90–140px) with their natural widths, 6–10px gaps, each project forming a run of four to eight frames preceded by its title in the same small text. The sheet fills the whole page width edge to edge with 16–20px margins. Hovering a run dims the others and shows that project's one-line description in a fixed position. A single enlarged frame may interrupt the sheet once per screen at four times the size.
direction.typography: One face. The name at display size on the first screen; everything else at one text size and one small size; hierarchy below the name comes from position and from a single brighter ink for titles.
direction.colour: Black or white ground, so the thumbnails are the only colour.
direction.imagery: Many images: at least 24 frames to make a sheet. They can be project photographs from the dealt set cropped to mixed ratios, or page captures of the work. Square corners, no captions on the frames.
direction.richness: Density and order. The mass of small images forms a texture; the strict rows keep it calm.
direction.pitfalls: With fewer than about 20 images it looks unfinished; choose another direction. Do not add a big headline above the sheet. On a phone the frames become two per row at a fixed height and each run scrolls sideways. Rows that run past the right edge read as clipped in screenshots and to most visitors: wrap the frames onto the next line, or end each row inside the grid.

hero.name: Lit strip, four corners
hero.blueprint: One near-black field with a single lit band. Four small pieces of text at 14px, medium weight, sit in the corners on 72px side margins and 44px top and bottom margins: the name top-left, one link top-right, one sentence saying what this is bottom-left (max 36ch), the single action as a text link bottom-right. Across the vertical middle runs one horizontal strip of photographs, 34vh tall (about 300px), each at its natural width with 10px gaps and square corners: eleven or more frames in a flex row wider than the viewport, so the first and last visible frames are cropped by the left and right edges. The frame nearest the centre is at full brightness; the others sit at filter: brightness(0.55) and brighten on hover or as they reach the centre. Under the centred frame, aligned to its left edge, its title is set in the same 14px text. The top quarter and the bottom quarter of the screen stay empty and dark. The strip scrolls sideways with overflow-x: auto and scroll-snap; never hijack vertical scroll.
hero.mobile: The strip stays a single sideways-scrolling row but grows to 46vh tall, so one frame and the cropped edges of its neighbours fill the width. The name and the link sit at the top on 20px margins; the sentence and the action stack bottom-left under the strip at 14px. Dark space remains above and below the strip, about 12% of the height each.
hero.headline: None at display size: the name at 14px in a corner and one sentence of up to 60 characters.

type.note: A light grotesque with open, slightly old-fashioned shapes; large headings look airy and the text weight beneath stays easy to read. Suits AI and research products, fashion houses and calm brand sites.

palette.name: Plum-black and pink
palette.note: Near-black and plum at the top and bottom bracket a white middle with navy-black text. Hot pink is reserved for primary buttons, bars in charts and map markers; it never fills a section.

photos.title: Objects
photos.note: single objects seen close: instruments, tools, cameras, books

motion.name: Drag row
motion.description: A row of large items wider than the screen that the visitor pulls sideways: native horizontal scrolling with scroll snapping, the first item aligned to the page margin and the last allowed to run off the edge so the row visibly continues. No carousel library, no arrows, no dots.

sections.name: Frame run, one lifted
sections.blueprint: Columns 1–3 are a nearly empty column: the heading (two to four words at 24–28px) at the top, a link under it, and one or two short notes at 15px much further down, each level with the frame it describes. Columns 4–12 hold a run of six to eight frames of the same subject at one fixed height of 30vh, with natural widths and 6px gaps: the whole view, a tight crop of the same thing, a detail, the reverse side. The run is allowed to leave the right edge. One frame is lifted out of the row: shown at 2.2 times the row height with its bottom aligned to the row's bottom (flex row, align-items: end), so it stands above the others. Under each frame, at 15px: a name on the left and a single fact on the right. Square corners, no captions on the images.
sections.mobile: The heading and link sit on top. The lifted frame comes first at full width. The rest of the run scrolls sideways beneath it at a fixed height of 34vw with 4px gaps and scroll-snap, bleeding off the right edge. Notes are listed under the run at 15px.

sections.name: Small proof beside text
sections.blueprint: One narrow module repeated four to six times down the page, never alternating sides. Each module is 640px wide at most and starts on the page's text margin (at about 22% of the viewport on an understated page). Left part: a flat panel 360px wide and 120 to 200px tall, one tone off the ground, radius 8px, holding one small exact demonstration: a cropped interface fragment at true size, or a tightly cropped photograph covering the panel. Right part, 20px away and top-aligned: a heading of one or two lines at 18px medium and two short paragraphs at 15px in the soft ink, in a column 250px wide. Panel heights vary with their content; text always hangs from the panel's top edge. 96–120px of empty ground between modules. The section heading is 24–28px, on the same left edge, 64px above the first module. In a column under 600px the text moves beneath its panel.
sections.mobile: Each module stacks: the panel at full width and natural height, then heading and paragraphs 16px below on the same left edge, at 17px and 15px. 64px between modules. Panels keep their true-size contents and crop from the right instead of scaling down.

sections.name: Drag row of moments
sections.blueprint: A story told left to right. Top row: the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, at the left margin; at the right margin two solid square buttons, 48px each, for back and forward. Directly beneath, a solid bar 6px tall spans the full width in a soft tone, with a full-ink segment showing how far the row has been scrolled. Then the row itself: six to nine columns, each 280px wide with 32px gaps, in a horizontally scrolling flex container with scroll-snap that bleeds off both viewport edges. Every column reads top to bottom: a one-line caption at 18px bold that carries the order in words ('We met', 'Two winters on', 'The move'), three lines at 15px in the soft ink, then 80–140px of empty space that varies per column, then a 4:5 portrait photograph. Because the spaces vary, the photographs' top edges rise and fall along the row.
sections.mobile: Columns are 72vw wide with 16px gaps, so the next one always shows at the right edge. The buttons are dropped; the 6px progress bar stays under the heading. The empty space inside columns shrinks to 32–64px but still varies from column to column.

sections.name: Two-ended rows, narrow column
sections.blueprint: A list in one narrow column, 520px wide, starting at 22% of the viewport width or centred. Every row is 34–38px tall with no box and nothing drawn between rows. Each row has two ends: at the left, a 16px round image (a face, a logo, a colour dot) followed after 8px by the name at 15–16px in full ink; at the far right of the column, a short value at 13px in the soft ink (a date, a price, a domain, an opening time) with tabular figures. Entries that need a sentence run to two lines at the left, and the value aligns with the first line. Groups are separated by 40px of space and begin with one plain word in the soft ink at the same size. A heading of two to four words at 24–28px in medium weight sits 32px above the first row. Holds 10–40 rows.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 44px tall for touch; the left image stays 16px. Long values wrap beneath the name at 13px, left-aligned with it, and the row grows. Group spacing is 32px.

sections.name: Recognition as a table
sections.blueprint: Awards, press mentions or credits set as a four-column table with no lines. The heading is two or three words at about 5vw, stepped over two lines with the second line indented by two columns, and occupies columns 1–7. The table begins 72px below and spans columns 1–12 on a fixed grid: year in columns 1–2, project or title in 3–6, awarding body or publication in 7–10, the award itself in 11–12, right-aligned. Rows are set at 16–17px with 14px of padding above and below; every second row carries a background tone one step from the ground, running the full table width, which replaces rules. Year groups are separated by one blank row, and the year is printed only on the first row of its group. Use a real `<table>` with `border-collapse: collapse` and no borders.
sections.mobile: The heading drops to 11vw. Each table row becomes a two-line block: title on the first line in the full ink, then body and award on the second in the softer ink. The year stands once as a 22px figure above its group. Alternate blocks keep the background tone.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Gil Huybrecht
references.idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
references.hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
references.type: One neo-grotesk at a single size, about 16px (1.1vw), medium-bold with tight tracking, white on black, for everything: name, lists, labels, numbers, footer. There is no headline; hierarchy comes only from column position and indentation.
references.colour: #000000 #fcfcfc #272727 #8a8a8a — Pure black with white text; the only colour is whatever appears inside the screenshot thumbnails. Inactive toggle words drop to mid-grey on a dark grey chip.
references.imagery: Miniature full-page captures of the designer's client sites, uncropped at natural aspect ratios, square corners, no frames or shadows, about 190px wide, sitting directly on black.
references.layout: Seven equal columns with 14px gutters and margins for the whole page. Thumbnails align to columns but not to rows: each hangs from its own label at its own height, so bottoms are ragged. Projects flow continuously and wrap across rows.

sections.description: A seven-column field of screenshot thumbnails on black. Each project is a consecutive run of four to six thumbnails; the project name sits above the first, and every thumbnail carries its sequence number right-aligned above it in the same 16px white. Thumbnails keep their real proportions, so a row mixes 100px-tall and 280px-tall items with ragged bottoms and about 90px of black between rows. Runs break mid-row and continue on the next line with no divider.

View toggles. Two fixed chip pairs sit in the viewport's bottom corners: the left switches between a grid and a gallery view, the right between a normal and a novelty perspective mode. Each pair is a small dark-grey rounded rectangle containing two words, the active one white and the inactive grey, at the same 16px as all other text.

After about a screen of empty black, one band of text on the same seven columns: year and privacy link stacked at the left, then two columns of stacked social links, then two single links toward the right edge. Same size and weight as the header, no rule, no logo.

steal: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
Show projects as numbered runs of uncropped page screenshots at natural heights on a strict column grid, leaving the bottoms ragged.
Leave a deliberate 300px void between the text header and the first row of work so the lists read as a letterhead.
references.media: A contact-sheet wall: one fixed WebGL canvas draws about 84 full-page screenshots of client sites at a single 190px width and their native ratios, every page of each project in reading order. Once scrolled, every screen is about three rows, roughly 48% picture and 52% black, with text under 1% and the labels above each frame, never on it; there is no video.
references.motion: The preloader counts at about 13% a second for some 7-8s while the screenshot textures load, although the document loaded in 1.66s; then the first-row thumbnails rise into their slots in random order and a dark veil lifts. Lenis over a 4440px scroll proxy redraws the fixed wall with no pins or reveals; panel and hover moves use transform .75s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), and pictures fade over 1s ease-out on the phone.

references.name: Smallbits
references.idea: The icon set is the page: a full-viewport wall of the product with one docked card holding every word.
references.hero: The whole viewport is a black field tiled with white pixel icons, each drawn about 50px on a 112px pitch, nine rows deep; alternate rows shift half a cell so it reads as a brick pattern, and icons at the edges are cropped. There is no header. A white square-cornered card, 795×170px, is docked bottom-centre: a two-line 24px semibold sentence left, a black rectangular button right, a row of five grey links below. A third-party badge floats top-right. This single screen is the entire page.
references.type: Inter 600 at 24px, -0.02em, for the one sentence; Inter 16px semibold grey for links and button. Nothing exceeds 1.7vw — the pixel icons, not type, are the display element.
references.colour: #000000 #ffffff #9a9a9a #ff6154 — Strict black and white: white icons on black, black text on a white card, grey for secondary links. The only colour is the coral third-party badge.
references.imagery: About ninety visible pixel icons, each an 8×8 bitmap drawn at 50px in pure white with hard edges, tiled full-bleed and cropped at the viewport edges.
references.layout: One viewport, no scroll. A staggered icon grid fills the frame edge to edge; all words live in one docked card. On mobile the card becomes a full-width white block with a full-width button.

sections.description: Mobile restack, the only other state. The icon wall drops to five columns filling the top 73% of the screen; the card becomes a full-width white block at the bottom with the sentence on three lines at 18px, a full-width black button 78px tall, and five grey links spaced evenly on one line.

steal: Make the product the wallpaper: tile the full viewport with the assets at large size and skip a hero image entirely.
Offset alternate rows by half a cell so a regular grid reads as a pattern rather than a table.
Compress all copy, the CTA and the footer links into one docked card so the page never needs to scroll.

references.name: 21 Hrs On The Moon
references.idea: An explorable Apollo 11 landing site: a title screen where the word MOON sets behind the lunar horizon, then a draggable top-down surface map with hotspots and a mission timeline.
references.hero: Black starfield framed by thin bronze corner brackets; three small round icon buttons top-left. A centred composition 72% wide sits between two thin rules. The upper rule is interrupted by a small bold caps kicker; beneath it the four-letter title in bold geometric caps at 20.8vw spans the full width, light grey fading to transparent at its base. A grey cratered sphere rises from the bottom, its curved horizon overlapping the lower quarter of the letters. On the sphere: a two-line centred white sentence, with a mono-labelled mission name at far left and year at far right above the lower rule. A bracketed mono button sits centred at 82% height.
references.type: Futura Std Bold in uppercase at 300px with -0.03em tracking for the title, the same face near 28px for the kicker and 20px for the sentence; Akkurat Mono in tiny uppercase for labels, the button and map annotations. Roughly a 15x jump from title to sentence.
references.colour: #020202 #262626 #d8d8d8 #8a7361 #ffffff — Black and lunar greys with white type. A muted bronze appears only in the HUD brackets and translucent wedge markers on the map; archival photo thumbnails add small spots of colour.
references.imagery: A real-time 3D moon: curved horizon on the title screen, then a full-screen top-down cratered surface lit from one side. Small archival photos appear as thumbnail hotspots with bracketed corners; icons sit in outlined circles and squares.
references.layout: A single-screen application rather than a scrolling page: a centred title card, then a draggable map filling the viewport with hotspots at fixed coordinates. HUD brackets, icon buttons at top-left and a timeline ruler along the bottom persist throughout.

sections.description: Full-viewport top-down lunar surface in dark grey with fine crater relief. About ten hotspots are scattered over it: outlined circular icons for panoramas, each with a translucent bronze wedge showing the camera's field of view; small square icons for experiments; two photo thumbnails with corner brackets. Each has a tiny mono caps label to its right. One landmark gets a larger bold geometric caps label with a small triangle above it. A tiny mono hint sits top-centre.

Pinned along the bottom, a horizontal ruler spanning about 75% of the width: a thin baseline with short vertical ticks dividing eight equal segments, each labelled in two lines of tiny mono caps, a small triangle marking the current position and a clock readout at the left end. The current landmark's name in bold caps sits beneath it, half-cropped by the bottom edge of the screen.

steal: Let a 3D or photographic object physically overlap the bottom of giant title letters and fade the letters to transparent there, so the type sits inside the scene rather than on top of it.
Interrupt a thin horizontal rule with the small first line of the title, then close the block with a second rule carrying two labelled facts at its left and right ends.
Frame the viewport with four thin corner brackets in a muted metallic colour to turn a full-screen scene into a viewfinder.
references.media: The hero is all picture: a starfield and a rising moon sphere over the lower ~55%, with the title sunk into its horizon. After landing, a draggable top-down terrain map fills the whole screen, with 120x90 archival photo thumbnails as pins and translucent field-of-view wedges; no video on the surface, as footage and panoramas open from the hotspots.
references.motion: There is no document scroll: the first wheel step plays a landing in which the terrain lights up and the hotspots arrive in a stagger, labels after their icons, and from then on the wheel does nothing and the map is dragged instead. HUD items fade in and out on a uniform 400ms, with one opacity .3s cubic-bezier(.61,1,.88,1); no GSAP, and the page took 38s to reach network idle.
